meta_title: TigerTag: the open NFC standard for 3D-printing filament and resin
meta_description: TigerTag is the free, open NFC protocol that tells any reader the material, colour, print settings and remaining quantity of a filament spool or resin bottle, and proves it is genuine, fully offline.
og_title: TigerTag: one NFC chip, every machine
og_description: The free, open NFC standard for 3D-printing materials: material, settings, quantity and offline authenticity on one small chip.

what_title: What a TigerTag tells a reader
what_lead: Everything needed to print is on the chip itself. A reader that never reaches the network loses none of it.
what1_text: PLA, PETG, ABS, resin and hundreds more, with the brand and the product, from an open reference database.
what2_text: Up to three colours, and two aspects such as matte, silk, carbon or glow.
what3_text: Nozzle and bed temperatures, drying temperature and time, and the transmission distance used by HueForge.
what4_text: The initial and the remaining quantity, by weight, volume or length, updated as the spool is used.
what5_text: One chip on each flange, paired by a shared identifier: the spool is found from either side, and each tag knows it is 1 of 2 or 2 of 2.
what6_text: A TigerTag+ Certified chip carries an ECDSA-P256 signature that any reader checks offline: is this spool genuine?
types_lead: The same 144 bytes, read the same way. What changes is what the chip can promise.
t1_text: Everything needed to print, written by anyone: a brand, a maker, an app. Works fully offline.
t2_text: A TigerTag that carries a product id from the official catalogue: name, SKU, barcode and image resolve offline, and corrections reach the chip after it was written.
t3_text: A TigerTag+ signed by a certified manufacturer. The signature is bound to the chip's unique id, so a copied chip fails the check.
how_lead: A TigerTag is a plain NFC chip, never locked in write. The format is public, the tools are open source.
step1_text: A brand, a factory or a maker writes the material, colours, settings and quantity: 80 bytes of data on pages 0x04 to 0x17.
step2_text: A phone, a TigerPOD, a scale or a printer accessory reads the chip and decodes it with the open reference tables, offline.
step3_text: On a certified chip, the reader checks the signature on pages 0x18 to 0x27 against the public key shipped with the protocol.
step4_text: The remaining weight is written back as the spool is used. A brand's corrected settings reach a TigerTag+ in the field, without a recall.
layout_data_detail: type, product, material, aspects, brand, diameter, colours, quantity, temperatures, drying, timestamp, tag index
layout_sig_detail: ECDSA-P256 over the chip UID and pages 4 and 5; zeros on an unsigned chip
layout_link: The full byte layout in the specification
why1_text: An ECDSA-P256 signature, verified fully offline with a public key shipped with the protocol.
why2_title: A chip that is never thrown away
why2_text: Never locked in write: move it to the next spool, or give it a second life as a connected NFC tag.
why3_text: A brand publishes corrected settings; a compatible reader updates the chip in place. No recall.
why4_text: Owned by no printer maker and favouring no machine. The chip describes the material, not the device that reads it.
why5_text: An irrevocable, royalty-free right to implement it, in open source or proprietary products.
why6_text: The reference tables and the full product catalogue are public domain (CC0): embed them anywhere.

faq1_q: Which NFC chip does TigerTag use?
faq1_a: An NTAG213 or larger (NTAG215, NTAG216), ISO 14443-3. The layout fits the 144 bytes of the smallest one, so any larger chip works too.
faq2_a: Yes. Implementing the protocol requires no licence and no payment, in any product, open source or proprietary. Only the TigerTag mark on a product and signed chips require certification.
faq3_a: No. Material, colours, settings, quantity and the signature check are all read from the chip and the bundled reference tables. The API only adds extra detail.
faq4_q: How does a reader know a spool is genuine?
faq4_a: A TigerTag+ Certified chip carries an ECDSA-P256 signature of its unique id and product. The reader verifies it offline with the public key published with the protocol.
faq5_q: Can I reuse a TigerTag chip?
faq5_a: Yes. TigerTag chips are never locked in write: move one to another spool, or reuse it for anything an NFC tag can do.
faq6_q: My spools have Bambu Lab, Creality or QIDI chips. What about them?
faq6_a: Tiger Studio Manager links those maker chips to your inventory by their id, without decoding or rewriting them. You can also add a TigerTag next to them.
faq7_a: Through Tiger Studio Manager, TigerSpool and Tiger Touch: Bambu Lab, Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic, Snapmaker, FlashForge, Prusa, and Klipper or OctoPrint machines.
